note: Independent rejudgment against the complete private-AS paragraph of RFC 9234 Section 5: 'On egress from the Internet-facing AS, the OTC Attribute MUST NOT contain a value other than the Internet-facing ASN.' The requirement row is now unannotated: it retains the exact obligation, permanent id, level and section without the unsupported single-polarity exemption or a gap annotation incompatible with its existing positive tag. The sole tagged unit, TestOTCEgressStampLocalASN in internal/component/bgp/plugins/role/rfc9234_otc_test.go, supplies reachable unicast NLRI with no OTC and a locally configured downstream destination. It asserts exactly one operation whose decoded value is dest.LocalAS 64999, distinguished from source ASN 65001 and destination ASN 65002. This remains useful isolated proof of absent-OTC synthesis. OTCEgressFilter in internal/component/bgp/plugins/role/otc.go creates OTC only when it is absent and otherwise preserves the existing value. The tagged unit does not supply an already-present OTC carrying a wrong private or internal ASN at the Internet-facing boundary, so it cannot detect noncompliance in that part of the requirement. No negative polarity currently covers the requirement. The existing positive test and claim remain unchanged; removing the unsupported exemption exposes the genuine missing-negative finding rather than inventing coverage or retagging the test. This is a testing limitation and not an observed wire violation, a justification to rewrite arbitrary received OTC, or a whole-requirement conformance claim. No runtime or producer-break replay was run for this source rejudgment.
